query: In 2011, did Macao SAR, China count as a low-, lower-middle-, upper-middle- or high-income economy, and how far was it from the nearest dividing line? Use the income thresholds that applied to 2011 GNI per capita.

text.text: Identifies that the answer applies the World Bank country income classification: Atlas-method GNI per capita compared against the annual low / lower-middle / upper-middle / high income cut-offs.
text.accept: full = names the World Bank income classification by GNI per capita cut-offs; acceptable alternative: IDA / Paris Club eligibility lens built on the same income tiers; no = ranks by GDP per capita without cut-offs or by IMF advanced/emerging grouping

text.text: States the 2011 bracket: high-income (GNI per capita 54620 US dollars).
text.accept: full = bracket matches (high-income) and, for claim items, TRUE/FALSE verdict matches

data.text: Uses World Bank Atlas GNI per capita (current US dollars, NY.GNP.PCAP.CD) for 2011.

computation.text: Atlas-method GNI per capita of Macao SAR, China in 2011 = 54620 US dollars
computation.accept: full = within 3 percent (vintage revisions of the Atlas series)

computation.text: Distance to the nearest income cut-off (12475 US dollars) = +42145 US dollars
computation.accept: full = within tolerance; sign positive if above the cut-off

assembled_from: IMF External Debt Statistics Guide (2013) glossary: cut-offs for 2011
provenance.selection: drawn from 168 countries with 2011 Atlas GNI per capita at least 8 percent away from every cut-off (robust to data revision); seeded draw; one per country

gold_report_note: The classification rule is printed in the IMF guide (not a country report); nothing to withhold. Implementation check: same rule with the 2024 cut-offs reproduces the current World Bank grouping for 194 of 198 countries (wb_classifications.csv); the misses are within 1 percent of a cut-off.
distractors: GDP per capita at market prices
